passage:
Monday. During a quarrel over the cricket score, Vijay shouted, "At least I don't cry in the toilets when I miss the choir!" Sarita's mouth fell open. The whole line of children heard.

Tuesday. Vijay's dal sat untouched. First he practised saying, "You made me so angry," then stopped. She had not made him say it. His stomach twisted.

Thursday. He found Sarita by the water tank. "I'm sorry I told everyone your secret. It was mine to keep, and I broke it. No excuses." Sarita looked at her shoes. "I'm still upset," she said. "I don't know when I'll feel okay." Vijay nodded. "That's fair. I'll wait."

qa.q: What did Vijay shout during the quarrel over the cricket score?
qa.a: He shouted, "At least I don't cry in the toilets when I miss the choir!"

qa.q: What did Vijay realise on Tuesday about blaming Sarita?
qa.a: He realised she had not made him say it, so the blame was his own, and this made his stomach twist.

qa.q: What would you advise Vijay to do after Sarita says she is still upset?
qa.a: Give her time without pressing, and show through steady small actions that he can be trusted again.

qa.q: What might it be like for Sarita on Thursday at the water tank?
qa.a: She is probably still hurt and embarrassed because the whole line heard, so she needs time even though the sorry was honest.

grounding: A child lets out a friend's secret in a fight, feels awful, apologises without excuses and accepts that trust may take time.

passage:
The school bus was stuck in traffic for an hour, and everyone was hot and cranky. Shreya and Nikita were arguing about the window seat. Then Nikita snapped, "At least I don't still sleep with a teddy bear, Shreya!"
The whole bus laughed. Shreya went scarlet and turned to the window.
Nikita's stomach dropped. That was the secret Shreya had told her in Class 3.
When the bus finally reached school, Nikita caught up with her. "I'm really sorry. There's no excuse. I was angry, but that's my fault, not yours."
Shreya didn't look at her. "I need some time."
"Okay. I'll wait."

qa.q: What secret did Nikita shout on the bus?
qa.a: That Shreya still sleeps with a teddy bear.

qa.q: How did Nikita feel after she let the secret out?
qa.a: She felt awful and guilty, her stomach dropping.

qa.q: What did Nikita do right in her apology?
qa.a: She said sorry with no excuses, took responsibility and accepted that Shreya needed time.

qa.q: How might Shreya feel after Nikita apologises?
qa.a: Shreya is still hurt and embarrassed, needing time before trusting Nikita again.

grounding: A girl lets out her friend's secret in a fight and feels awful; she apologises without excuses and accepts trust will take time.

passage:
In the Chennai school canteen, Anjali and Lavanya argued over a group project. Anjali's voice rose. "Well, at least I didn't fail maths last term, Lavanya!"
The table went silent. Lavanya's face crumpled. Only Anjali had known.
Anjali felt sick. She wanted to say Lavanya had made her angry. But that was just an excuse.
After lunch she found Lavanya by the lockers. "I'm sorry. That was your secret, and I used it to hurt you. It was completely my fault."
Lavanya wiped her eyes. "I trusted you."
"I know. I'll understand if you need time."
Lavanya nodded slowly.

qa.q: Where did Anjali and Lavanya argue?
How did Anjali feel after revealing the secret?
qa.a: She felt sick and guilty, knowing she had hurt Lavanya.

qa.q: What did Anjali do that was honest?
qa.a: She apologised fully, took responsibility instead of blaming Lavanya for making her angry, and accepted that Lavanya might need time.

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel after Anjali's apology?
qa.a: Lavanya is still hurt but may begin to trust again because Anjali took full responsibility.

grounding: A girl reveals her friend's secret in a fight and feels awful; she apologises without excuses and accepts trust will take time.
